event.summary: The detach timeout test yields before establishing writer backpressure
event.detail:
# Detach timeout test does not establish its stalled-writer premise

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The rewritten terminal teardown test can pass without exercising the timeout that keeps a stuck host connection from holding a terminal socket open. Removing that timeout can therefore go undetected by the test named for it. This is a test-evidence defect; no shipped teardown failure is established here.

## Details
terminal.rs:1183-1195 replaces the old single send_input call with a loop of send_grid_input calls, polls it once, and treats any Pending as proof that the real writer queue is full. Each iteration now awaits both terminals.lock() and writer_tx.send() (client.rs:4111-4134). The pinned dependency is Tokio 1.53.2 (Cargo.lock). Its mutex acquires the batch semaphore (tokio-1.53.2/src/sync/mutex.rs:434-455,655-663); bounded Sender::send reserves through the same semaphore (sync/mpsc/bounded.rs:816-824,1116-1119,1272-1302); each successful Acquire poll consumes one cooperative budget unit (sync/batch_semaphore.rs:617-662). The task's poll budget is 128 (task/coop/mod.rs:105-117), and poll_proceed returns Pending when exhausted (:291-365). Thus this loop can exhaust its budget after at most 64 iterations while the writer's queue capacity is itself 64 (client.rs:173,1779). The successful oneshot receive returning the Attach reply has already consumed a budget unit before the loop (client.rs:2990-2992; Tokio sync/oneshot.rs:1317-1375), leaving at most 127, so the first Pending can occur after at most 63 input frames: before the queue fills. The test runs in an ordinary current-thread Tokio runtime, without unconstrained polling (farhelm-testtrace-macros/src/lib.rs:55-64; farhelm-testtrace/src/lib.rs:995-1013,1126-1142). The writer can dequeue additional frames when the test next yields, adding spare slots.

At terminal.rs:1197-1204 the test neither checks writer capacity nor checks that detach_bounded consumed WS_TEARDOWN_GRACE. Its release_upstream task (client.rs:2499-2519) can enqueue Detach into a spare slot and finish immediately. The peer is released only afterward, so receiving Detach proves eventual notification but not that a caller timeout occurred or that notification survived it. This violates the test's stated contract (:1116-1122) and the test-authoring requirement ‘Assert the fixture premise before the action or measurement that depends on it.’ A source-level repair is to establish exhausted writer capacity explicitly (for example, using the existing writer-capacity reservation seam) and assert the virtual grace actually elapsed before releasing the peer.

Suggested bucket: other, because the established consequence is missing maintainer test coverage. Confidence: confirmed by source/dependency contract analysis; no runtime tests or reproductions were performed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources were not searched. Could-be-highest: no; this finding establishes no shipped security, data, process, or user-owned-work loss. Caveats: the previous send_input version also assumed Pending meant capacity pressure, but it charged one semaphore acquisition per chunk instead of two; this rewrite introduces an unavoidable cooperative-budget boundary at or before the 64-slot capacity and removes the source argument that the single poll filled it. The precise dynamic frame count is not claimed as observed.

event.detail:
# Detach timeout test does not establish its stalled-writer premise

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The rewritten terminal teardown test can pass without exercising the timeout that keeps a stuck host connection from holding a terminal socket open. Removing that timeout can therefore go undetected by the test named for it. This is a test-evidence defect; no shipped teardown failure is established here.

## Details
The required boundary is explicit at terminal.rs:1116-1122: the peer stops reading, input fills the bounded writer queue, detach_bounded must return at its grace, and only after that may the released peer receive the independently owned Detach. Eventual notification alone does not establish the timeout or survival across caller timeout. At :1183-1195 the changed loop polls send_grid_input once and calls every Pending writer backpressure; :1197-1204 never checks capacity or elapsed virtual grace.

Synthesis verified the exact dependency and polling scope. Cargo.lock pins Tokio 1.53.2. farhelm-testtrace-macros/src/lib.rs:248-259 selects CurrentThread for this start_paused test. farhelm-testtrace/src/lib.rs:995-1013 and :1126-1142 create a fresh ordinary runtime and block_on the test body. Tokio runtime/scheduler/current_thread/mod.rs:180-253 creates/takes that runtime's scheduler core; :815-834 wraps each root-future poll in coop::budget. task/coop/mod.rs:105-155 gives that outer poll 128 units and restores the previous budget only when the outer closure returns. terminal.rs:1191-1194 uses std::future::poll_fn and calls Future::poll directly; it neither creates a fresh Tokio task nor calls budget/unconstrained. An inner Pending is converted into Ready(true), so this manual poll does not itself leave the ordinary root cooperative scope.

Attach consumes budget in that same scope: client.rs:2990-2992 successfully polls its oneshot receiver; Tokio sync/oneshot.rs:1317-1334 calls poll_proceed and made_progress on successful receipt. The success return through client.rs:4054-4069 and :3975-3976 has no subsequent await or scope reset before terminal.rs:1183-1194. start_grid_flow uses a synchronous gauge mutex, creates a false watch and starts an observer; it does not renew cooperative budget (client.rs:861-898,4155-4178).
